verdict.text: The result matched the chances: 0.72 xG to 1.96.

howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 62.0% of the ball and 63.7% of the passing in the opposition half, against a season average of 62.8%.
They took 7 shots (4 on target) worth 0.72 xG, about 0.10 per shot; Leeds had 16 shots worth 1.96 xG.
The match changed after half-time: Spurs' xG difference went from +0.03 in the first half to -1.17 in the second.
Momentum: Leeds on top, 6–16'; Spurs on top, 23–30'; Spurs on top, 32–39'; Leeds on top, 45.5–52'; Leeds on top, 71–85'.
In short: dominated the ball, pinned the opponent back, short, patient passing.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-3-3 against Leeds's 3-4-2-1 (1 change from the Crystal Palace game, switching from 4-2-3-1).
The result matched the chances: 0.72 xG to 1.96.
Compared with their other league games, Spurs conceded more (1.96 xG vs 1.11 xG), got into the box less (18 vs 33), created better-quality chances (0.10 vs 0.08), went long more often (4.3% vs 3.3%).
Bentancur was the biggest attacking threat (0.38 xG + xA); Pedro Porro won the ball back most often (3 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 62% of the ball (season average 63%), completing 444 of 531 passes (84%).
64% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), below their usual 71%. They spent long spells camped in Leeds's half.
52% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (230 own half, 214 opposition half): a balanced split between building and attacking.
Long balls made up 4.3% of accurate passes (in line with the season's 3.3%), with 34% of long balls finding a teammate.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 7 shots (4 on target) worth 0.72 xG, 0.10 per shot; the season average is 0.08 per shot, so the chances were better quality than usual.
5 shots came from inside the box and 2 from outside (29% from distance).
Spurs created 1 big chance and missed 1 (season average 2.4).
18 touches in Leeds's box, well below the season average of 33; Leeds had 21 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 0.65 (74%), fast breaks 0.16, set pieces 0.07. 4 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 0 from 0.72 xG: 0.7 fewer than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 1.42 xGOT against 0.72 xG before the shot: the finishing placed shots better than average.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 3.6 Leeds passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.1. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was Spurs' usual pressing level.
15 tackles won and 4 interceptions (season averages 17.8 and 7.9); 33 clearances and 5 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 43, Leeds 65 (40% for Spurs); 45% of aerial duels won.
Leeds managed 16 shots worth 1.96 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.11 xG) and 4 big chances.

phases.title: Transitions and set pieces
read: Fast breaks: Spurs had 1 shot on the break (0.16 xG); Leeds had 1 (0.40 xG), against a season average of 1.2 shots conceded on the break.
Set pieces: 2 Spurs shots (0.07 xG, 0 goals); Leeds 9 (1.23 xG, 1 goal). Corners: 4–6.

flow: First half: 0.22 xG for, 0.19 against (0–0). Second half: 0.67 for, 1.84 against (0–1). The balance shifted away from Spurs after half-time.
Spells on top (momentum index): Leeds 6–16'; Spurs 23–30'; Spurs 32–39'; Leeds 45.5–52'; Leeds 71–85'.
